My family has farmed this land for generations. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer corn — that's just what you do in Quzhou. The government extension station pushes the same rotation, my neighbors do it, and I know it. I'm not going to experiment with something unfamiliar when I have a wife and two kids depending on the harvest.

I have about 10 mu of land. I'll grow wheat in the winter season and corn on the same land in summer. Same as last year.

For wheat, I'll use the Jimai variety — the seed dealer in town stocks it and it performs well here. I put down compound fertilizer as a base before planting, then urea at jointing stage. My father used to apply less but yields dropped, so I apply a bit more nitrogen now. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at jointing, at heading, and once more during grain fill if the well water holds. That's four times. I'll spray herbicide after emergence and probably one fungicide pass in spring when the weather gets humid.

For corn, I plant right after the wheat harvest in June, no-till, straight into the stubble — saves time and the moisture stays in the ground. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, it's reliable. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and chase with urea when the corn is knee-high. Summer rains help but I'll irrigate two or three times depending on how dry it gets.

Pesticides — I'll spray for corn borer once, maybe twice if I see damage.
